info.title: TroSky Backend
info.description: TroSky: Smart Public Transport Platform for Ghana — backend API. Monetary values are GHS minor units (pesewas). All timestamps are UTC unless explicitly documented otherwise.

get.description:
Process is up and able to serve requests at all (no dependency checks).

Kubernetes uses this to decide whether to restart the pod.

Process is ready to serve traffic: dependent services are reachable.

Kubernetes uses this to decide whether to route traffic to the pod.

Verbose health/version info. Restricted: disabled entirely in
production (``EXPOSE_HEALTH_DETAILS=false``) and never returns secrets,
credentials, or infrastructure internals — only booleans and version
metadata already visible on the public OpenAPI schema.

post.description:
Register a passenger, driver, or fleet-owner account. Never creates
an administrator account — see README security notes.

Verify an OTP for the given purpose. For ``registration`` /
``phone_verification`` / ``email_verification``, this also marks the
corresponding contact detail as verified.

Request a new OTP for a given target and purpose (registration,
login, phone/email verification, or password reset).

The target may be written in any form (``0241234567`` or
``+233241234567``). A code is only sent to a registered account; for
any other target the response is identical but nothing is sent. When
the server sends codes by email (``OTP_DELIVERY_CHANNEL=email``), the
code goes to the account's email address whatever channel is asked for.
Authenticate with a phone number or email + password.

Passwordless login: complete with a code previously requested via
``POST /auth/resend-otp`` with ``purpose=login``.
Rotate the refresh token and issue a new access/refresh token pair.
Log out the current device (revokes the current session only).
Log out every device (revokes all sessions for this account).

Send a 6-digit password reset code to the account behind
``identifier`` (a phone number or email). Always the same answer, whether
or not such an account exists. Then call ``/password/reset`` with the
code.

Set a new password with the code ``/password/forgot`` sent --
``{"target", "code", "new_password"}``, where ``target`` is the phone or
email the code was requested for -- or with an older long ``token``.
Signs out every session on success.

post.description:
Create this account's driver verification profile and grant it the
``driver`` role (status starts ``pending``; see
``/api/v1/admin/drivers/pending`` for the review flow).

Any signed-in account may call this — that is what lets one TroSky
login be a passenger and a driver at once. The role takes effect
immediately: ``get_current_principal`` reloads roles from the database
on every request, so the existing access token keeps working.

get.description:
Trips a passenger can take, where they would board each one, and what
it costs from there.

The pickup defaults to the passenger's GPS position: send
``pickup_latitude``/``pickup_longitude`` and every stop within walking
distance becomes a candidate boarding point. Send ``origin_stop_id``
instead, or as well, when the passenger has chosen a pickup by hand;
a manual choice always overrides the coordinates.

Trips already on the road are included: a trotro picks people up along
its route. ``has_passed_pickup`` says when it is too late to catch one,
and ``vehicle_eta_to_pickup_minutes`` how far away it is otherwise.

schema.description: A pickup the passenger chose by hand. Always wins over GPS coordinates.

get.description:
Seat layout for a trip's assigned vehicle, with real-time
availability reflecting active (held or confirmed) reservations.

Bookings waiting for this driver to accept or decline them, the
nearest deadline first. A booking still unanswered at ``expires_at``
goes to another vehicle; the passenger pays only once it is accepted.

post.description:
Take the trip you were assigned. Starting it, or accepting a booking
on it, also counts as accepting it.

Turn the trip down, before it starts. You are taken off it and the
operations team assigns another driver.
Take this passenger: they are asked to pay now. Idempotent.

Turn this booking down. It goes to another vehicle going the same
way if one has seats; otherwise the passenger is told, uncharged.

This passenger got off -- at their stop or before it. Their seat is
free for the rest of the route from now on. Passengers are also marked
off automatically when the vehicle reaches the stop they booked to.

Idempotent: calling this again while the trip is already in progress
(by the same driver) simply returns the current trip state.

Idempotent: calling this again after the trip has already completed
(by the same driver) simply returns the current trip state.

A driver's phone pushes a GPS ping while the trip is in progress.
Restricted to the trip's actively assigned driver, same guard as
start/pause/resume/end/validate.

Boards a passenger: verifies the scanned QR code's signature, that
it actually belongs to this trip, and that it hasn't already been used,
expired, or been revoked — then marks it validated. Restricted to the
trip's actively assigned driver, same guard as start/pause/resume/end.

get.description:

the trip's assigned driver may see it (403 otherwise). ``boarded``
becomes true once the passenger's ticket is scanned with
``POST /driver-trips/{trip_id}/tickets/validate``. Phone numbers are
masked.

schema.title: Response List Trip Passengers Api V1 Driver Trips  Trip Id  Passengers Get

get.description:
What this trip's passengers paid, per seat and per payment channel.
Only the trip's assigned driver may see it (403 otherwise). Amounts are
fares, TroSky's platform fee excluded.

post.description:
Reserve one or more seats on a trip.

The booking first waits for the trip's driver (or an admin) to accept it:
status ``awaiting_acceptance``, with ``expires_at`` the deadline for an
answer. Unanswered or declined, it is moved to another vehicle from the
same pickup to the same destination (the passenger is notified) or, with
none, ends. Once accepted it is ``pending``: pay before the new
``expires_at`` (``SEAT_RESERVATION_HOLD_SECONDS``) or the seats are
released.

get.description: Your bookings, each with a short summary of its trip.

schema.description: true: trips still ahead -- departing now or later, or under way (soonest first). false: trips behind you (most recent first). Omit for both (newest booking first).
schema.title: Upcoming

get.description:
Vehicles leaving soon from where this booking's ride ended (or will
end), with a seat free, for carrying on the journey. The passenger is

schema.title: Response List Onward Trips Api V1 Bookings  Booking Id  Onward Trips Get

post.description:
Cancels a booking. If the trip hasn't started yet, this is decided
immediately (refund-eligible if the booking was already paid); once
boarding/departure has begun it's queued for admin review instead.

A refund-eligible cancellation only opens a ``RefundRequest`` here —
actually releasing money still needs a separate admin approval
(``POST /admin/refund-requests/{id}/approve``), never happens
automatically as a side effect of the passenger's own cancel call.

Initiates payment for a held booking. Wallet payments are debited
and confirmed synchronously; every other channel returns a
``processing`` payment that is later confirmed by that channel's
webhook (``POST /payments/webhooks/{channel}``) — never by this
response.

get.description:
One ticket per booked seat, issued automatically once the booking is
confirmed (see ``BookingService.confirm_booking``) — empty until then.

schema.title: Response List Booking Tickets Api V1 Bookings  Booking Id  Tickets Get

post.description:
Rates the trip once the booking has completed — see
``TripService.end_trip``, the only thing that ever moves a booking to
``COMPLETED``. ``score`` is the overall rating; ``safety``,
``cleanliness``, ``professionalism`` and ``timeliness`` are optional.

Manually re-polls the provider for a payment stuck pending — the
passenger-facing fallback for a delayed webhook (ownership-checked via
``get_payment`` first; the sync call itself trusts the id after that).

get.description:
Newest first. ``reference_type`` narrows to one kind of entry --
``trip_earning`` lists a driver's earnings.

post.description:
Requests a payout of the caller's own wallet balance to a mobile
money number. The wallet is not debited yet — only once an admin
approves the request (``POST /admin/withdrawals/{id}/approve``).

get.description: For the badge on the bell icon.

Messages from TroSky support about your complaint, oldest first. Each

schema.title: Response List Complaint Messages Api V1 Complaints  Complaint Id  Messages Get

post.description:
Report an incident on a trip the caller is part of. Add a photo
afterwards with ``POST /incidents/{incident_id}/photo``.

Attach a photo of the scene to an incident you reported. An incident
holds one photo: uploading again replaces it.

Triggers an emergency alert for the caller's own participation in
this trip and immediately SMSes every registered emergency contact —
never gated by notification preferences (see
``SafetyService._notify_emergency_contacts``).

Emergency alert when the caller is not on a trip (the Home screen's
SOS button). Send the phone's position: with no trip it is the only
clue to where they are. Emergency contacts are texted straight away,
exactly as for an SOS during a trip.

patch.description:
Change the fields sent. Moving a stop re-measures distances along
every active route that uses it. 409 STOP_CODE_TAKEN on a duplicate
code.

delete.description:
Retire a stop: it disappears from search and new bookings; past
bookings keep it. 409 STOP_IN_USE while an active route uses it.

patch.description:
Change the name, length or duration. A new length or duration
re-measures the distance and time to each stop. 409 ROUTE_NAME_TAKEN on
a duplicate name.

delete.description:
Retire a route and its timetable. 409 ROUTE_HAS_ACTIVE_TRIPS while it
still has trips scheduled or under way -- cancel or finish them first.
